title: 8th Sitting of second session of 2025
summary: The sitting ran from 09:01 to 10:33. Members held the preliminary debate on a government bill to amend the Attorney General's Office Act (Law 8/2025), which was passed only recently: government-side members said amendments are routine, while opposition MDP members questioned why a new law needed changing so soon. Debate then moved to a motion from the Kanditheemu member asking for fair overtime pay and working conditions for teachers and health workers, where speakers on both sides backed the idea but traded blame over past and present governments. No vote was recorded in this part, and the Speaker closed by reminding members to keep their speeches respectful and to attend committees, and announced the next sitting for 30 June 2025 at 09:00.

items.title: Debate on a motion from the Kanditheemu member Ameen Faisal on overtime pay and fair working conditions for education and health workers
items.outcome: debated; unfinished when the sitting ended at 10:33

speakers.name: Abdul Gafoor Moosa
positions: On the bill: said an Attorney General's Office law passed less than a year ago should not already need amending, and urged the government to send complete, well-prepared bills.
On the motion: backed it, citing pay rises under the previous MDP government (teachers MVR 12,000 to 21,000, nurses MVR 9,000 to 18,000).
Criticised the present government over unbuilt housing, unfinished projects and corruption concerns, and challenged its blaming of earlier governments.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Said amending laws soon after they start operating is normal, and saw no need to use more time as the bill drew no objection from the MDP.
Backed the overtime motion, saying overtime is capped at 10% of basic salary, and expected the 2026 budget to address teachers' and nurses' concerns.
Criticised the previous MDP-led government's record on revenue, borrowing and reserves.

speakers.name: Ali Fazad
positions: Introduced the government bill, saying it clarifies the Attorney General's Office responsibilities and conditions for state lawyers, and adjusts some staff pay and benefit rules.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Said a bill passed in the last term was already being amended again, and noted laws such as the Tourism Act had been amended several times.
Called on the government and Majlis to study laws properly before passing them, to avoid repeated corrections.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Said it is difficult to debate a bill amended a day after being passed, and that the Majlis time and ministers' workload were not producing visible results.
Raised a collapsed school boundary wall on Neellaidhoo as an example of unresolved local problems.

speakers.name: Ahmed Nazim
positions: Said the amendment is small, and that the Attorney General's Office has trouble hiring good lawyers within the civil service pay structure.
Said delays in bills reaching the Majlis hold up the work of committees and the House.

speakers.name: Hussain Shareef
positions: Said laws are routinely amended and opposition criticism of the bill was misplaced.
Referred to a Supreme Court ruling on MVR 23 million and said the previous MDP government left heavy national debt.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Said amending laws is a normal part of lawmaking everywhere.
Said the previous MDP government had about MVR 210 billion in revenue and loans and asked what it delivered.

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: Said the Judiciary Committee should handle bills more carefully, and welcomed some amendments while wanting control over hiring at the Attorney General's Office.
Rejected the claim that members leave early without working, saying committees keep meeting.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Hussain
positions: Supported the motion, saying teachers who finish a master's degree wait years for pay progression under civil service rules.
Said a teacher spends roughly 35 hours a month on extra work, and criticised the 2022 civil service changes under the MDP government.

speakers.name: Mohamed Musthafa Ibrahim
positions: Supported the motion as a former teacher, saying the 2022 pay framework capped overtime at 10% and cut pay on holiday days.
Called for the 10% overtime cap to be removed so teachers' extra work is fairly paid.

speakers.name: Hassan Zareer
positions: Supported the motion but asked what education and health spending, now much larger than five years ago, has actually improved.
Called for an education master plan and for better-planned hospitals and staffing, noting a shortage of trained special-needs teachers.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: Supported the motion, saying teachers and health workers deserve fair pay but the economy is stretched by loan repayments.
Called for investigation of money lost in past governments, including state company spending.

decisions: The Speaker announced the Social Committee's deadline for the Animal Handling and Welfare bill as 23 July 2025.
Debate on the Attorney General's Office Act amendment bill took place, with no vote recorded in this part.
Debate on the overtime pay motion for education and health workers was left unfinished at the end of the sitting.
The next sitting was set for 30 June 2025 at 09:00.
